system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every negotiated point. Three problems need the most attention:

1. **Fraud is not carved out.** The Seller's general provisions would apply caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which captures fraud.
2. **Title is folded into the general regime**, and their only title evidence is the Company's own register.
3. **The Update conflicts with their own Disclosure Letter.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed", but DL §2 says no consent or condition evidence has been given. The Update proposes a post-Completion Riverlark release, but DL §3 says the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists.

We should not concede any fallback position. No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for the 20% cap or the 18-month period.

---

## 1. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. | Reject and restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Treat the Seller's 20% as their opening, not a landing point. Do not signal that 20% is available. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Their figure is 5x ours. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | Reject both the size (5x ours) and the deductible mechanic. Together with the de minimis, this materially erodes the protection. |
| **General time limit (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. | Reject and restate 24 months. |
| **"Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Blanket default | Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories stay separate, with no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This drafting device quietly pulls specific indemnities, covenants, payment obligations, Tax and IP into the general cap, basket and time limit. Reverse the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general, "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject firmly. "Administrative simplicity" does not justify capping title to the asset we are buying at 20% of price. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Non-negotiable.** As drafted, this would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims and exclude reliance on fraudulent misrepresentation. Insert an express carve-out across cl 9.3, 12, 12.8, 13 and 20.5. No one on our side can trade this away. |
| **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN** | Do not accept that they are settled. Record that both remain open and are not resolved by the general regime. We are not assuming unlimited liability either way; these are for separate negotiation. |

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure (Sched 7; DL §1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is exactly the deemed disclosure our playbook rejects.
- Delete §1.1 and §1.2. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter.
- The letter numbering jumps from [1.2] to [1.4]. Ask for confirmation that no §1.3 has been omitted or is intended.
- The letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. We are now in November. Require an updated letter, and specify which disclosures (if any) may qualify warranties repeated at Completion.

**DL §1.4 (no admission).** This is a standard no-admission statement and can be tolerated in principle. It must not be read as diluting the factual content of specific disclosures. For example, DL §2, §3 and §5 are clear factual statements of what has *not* happened, and we will rely on them.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The clause excludes any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records. This is a blanket exclusion plus constructive knowledge, which the playbook rejects.
- Delete it.
- If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the Seller's *actual* knowledge, through named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry.
- It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Specific transaction issues

**Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL §2).** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m), with a change-control consent clause (cl 11.2) and conditions (cl 11.3).
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on *delivery* of written consent. The playbook rejects both.
- The Update says the consent is "addressed", but DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. Point out this inconsistency.
- Require a Completion condition, not waivable by the Seller, for an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent, plus documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met before Completion. The obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours.

**Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL §3).** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. DL §3 confirms it is unpaid and no discharge exists. A release "following Completion" means Completion would trigger change-control under a live, secured facility.
- Require a current payout letter and direct repayment from Completion funds into the funds flow.
- Require executed, effective security releases (including any PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- Any post-Completion release would need an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval. We do not have that approval, so do not offer this.
- Confirm the amount is treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

**Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL §5).** The bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but omits them from the funds flow. DL §5 confirms they are absent and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- The playbook prohibits silently excluding these amounts. If they are payable by the Company, an unitemised "matter for the Seller" statement does not protect us.
- Require either:
  - a specific funds-flow line item covering AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs, paid through payroll at Completion; or
  - an express Seller-funded mechanism, with the amount deducted from the price as a debt-like item and backed by a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs. Do not assume a figure.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4).** Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which the Seller itself says is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. It does not cover loss from the Company not owning or being unable to use the materials, or third-party claims.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and use, infringement claims, and the cost of obtaining an assignment.
- Keep the SOW3 cure: pay the outstanding fee, obtain a confirmatory assignment, and deliver the materials. Ideally this happens pre-Completion, with evidence.
- Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as either confirmed owing or confirmed paid until it is verified.

**DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sched 6; DL §6).** A download link to around 1,240 records was sent to an unintended external address.
- The Seller calls it "not expected to be material", but its own DL says access, scope and notification obligations are unestablished and the investigation is preliminary.
- Reject the materiality characterisation, but do not overstate the position either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure.
- Require log preservation, completion of the investigation, and regular updates to the Buyer before Completion.
- Require Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
- Require a specific indemnity (or equivalent) for losses arising from the incident, outside the general limitations. The disclosure must not exclude claims about it.

**Sandbar renewals (DL §8).** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) are recorded in DD-008 and DD-011.
- Do not accept the Seller's "ordinary-course" label at face value. We also should not automatically classify the amount as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- Ask for the contracts, timing, whether each renewal is committed or terminable, accrual treatment, and the business rationale. Then decide on treatment (Debt, working capital, warranty or none) once that information is in.

**Title (DL §10).** The only evidence is the Company's own register (DD-012), which DL §10 itself acknowledges.
- Require independent evidence: ASIC extract, share certificates, constitution, board and shareholder approvals, encumbrance/PPSR searches, the Seller's authority to sell, and releases of any share security (note Riverlark).
- Title warranties sit in the Fundamental regime (see §1).

**Lower-priority items: confirm, don't overreact.**
- **Lease (DL §7):** a notification obligation only. Diarise it and make it a Completion deliverable or a covenant.
- **Mossvale (DL §9):** an assignment restriction that does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Have counsel confirm there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Restate the playbook positions in full:**
   - 25% / AUD 6.0m cap
   - AUD 5,000 de minimis
   - AUD 50,000 tipping basket
   - 24-month general claims period
   
   No fallback is authorised. Any move to 20% or 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft.
2. **Fraud carve-out is non-negotiable.** Exclude fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.
3. **Separate the regimes.** Title and capacity get a 100% cap, at least 6 years, and sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Record that Tax and IP remain open.
4. **Disclosure:** strike the general data-room, register and public-record disclosure; require specific fair disclosure and an updated letter.
5. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier should cover only named-person Seller knowledge after reasonable enquiry, and never title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
6. **Bluefen:** require a hard Completion condition for effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only. Flag the inconsistency between the Update and the Disclosure Letter.
7. **Riverlark:** require a payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. Do not offer a post-Completion release.
8. **Bonuses:** require AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or an express Seller-funded deduction with an indemnity.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, obtain a confirmatory assignment, and verify the AUD 180,000.
10. **DD-006:** reject the "not material" label without assuming a breach. Require preservation, investigation, updates, consultation on notification, and specific protection.
11. **Sandbar:** request the underlying information before deciding treatment. No automatic Debt classification.
12. **Title:** obtain independent verification beyond DD-012.
13. **Housekeeping:** request an updated Disclosure Letter, explain the missing §1.3, and confirm the lease and Mossvale positions.

I'd suggest a cover note to Seller counsel that leads with points 2, 3 and 6. Those carry the greatest risk, and the inconsistency between the Seller's own documents gives us a clean basis for pushing back.
=== END ADVICE ===
